title: RAW UNREVIEWED: al-Qalqashandi’s additive letter-value packets, source-bound Muhammad example
summary: A manually verified historical example replaces each source letter by an Arabic letter packet carrying its numerical value: Muhammad becomes LI | BW | LI | AJ, with packet sums40,8,40,4. Different packets for the same value are expressly permitted. This is source evidence and an incomplete whole-message channel, not a22-sign adaptation, native interpretation, selected test or score.

historical_direction_and_example.quote_location: IX232, final printed line; undotted final ya appears in the old print. The normalized logical packet sequence below uses ي. Vertical bars are editorial packet annotations, not claimed historical extra marks.
historical_direction_and_example.roman_labels: LI | BW | LI | AJ. W denotes waw; these are letter labels, not inferred pronunciations.
historical_direction_and_example.source_operation: Write letters instead of the letter-number; the passage explains that lam+ya carry40, ba+waw8, lam+ya40 again, alif+jim4, thus returning M H M D. It expressly allows using other letters carrying these same numbers.
historical_direction_and_example.inverse: Given the same numeric convention AND the intended packet boundaries, add the letters in a packet and recover the letter with that number. This is a reconstruction of the stated arithmetic, not a claim that the text provides an exhaustive decoder/framing specification.
historical_direction_and_example.individual_weights_boundary: The familiar decomposition L30+Y10, B2+W6, A1+J3 is consistent with the displayed sums; the individual numbers are not all printed inIX232–233. Do not treat this note as a primary verification of the complete28-weight table.
historical_direction_and_example.numeric_set_boundary: The standard set{1..9,10,20,..90,100,200,..900,1000}, positivity, uniqueness of all28 values and maximum1000 must be declared as an additional precisely sourced convention before using them in an exhaustive test. This block establishes the four displayed target numbers only. III22 establishes an order, not the numeric assignment.
historical_direction_and_example.no_unlicensed_operations: No subtraction, signed value, modulo reduction or rolling state is described in this displayed rule. Excluding all such operations is a faithful narrow reconstruction of this example, not a claim that the entire historical treatise forbids other ciphers.

human_rule_and_cost.purpose: Conceal ordinary language correspondence by arithmetic substitutions, including alternative spellings of the same source letter. The reader must already know the language and the agreed numerical convention; the mechanism supplies no word meanings.
human_rule_and_cost.writer: For a source letter, know its numerical value; choose a letter packet that carries that value; preserve letter order between packets. The one-word example is hand-executable. No historical deterministic packet-choice policy or probability law was found in this passage.
human_rule_and_cost.reader: Recognize packet limits, sum the packet letters under the shared table, then read the recovered sequence in the known language.
human_rule_and_cost.learning: A shared alphabet-value table, arithmetic, source literacy and an agreed packet/word framing practice. No giant whole-word lexicon is required by the arithmetic, but ordinary lexical knowledge remains necessary.
human_rule_and_cost.unknown_words: A new name over the agreed source alphabet can in principle be written letterwise. Unsupported signs, diacritics, punctuation, nonalphabetic numbers and orthographic variants need additional declared treatment; this passage does not pay those costs.
human_rule_and_cost.boundaries: The example visually separates four packets for one source word. It does not show a multiword message that distinguishes packet separation from source-word separation. The later word-separator sentence belongs to another cipher subsection and cannot silently resolve this two-level issue.
human_rule_and_cost.line_handling: No complete rule for line continuation or packet splits is provided here. No invisible reset is inferred.
human_rule_and_cost.writing_length: No requirement of exactly two letters per packet is stated universally. A positive additive realization of value1 cannot use two positive terms; a universal two-sign-per-letter rule would therefore be an added restriction, not this historical example.
human_rule_and_cost.completeness: Arithmetic letter-channel retained; complete practical message framing, full numeric table and22-working-sign realization remain unprovided. This is not a complete candidate Voynich writer.
